overarching_objective: The student can confidently discuss their daily learning habits, study tools, and how they balance studying English with their job as a primary school teacher.
final_task: A guided discussion where the student verbally presents their ideal weekly study plan to the tutor, explaining their goals, preferred study spaces, and how they manage their time around teaching and family life.

lessons.objective: The student can describe their daily schedule and identify when they have time to study.
lessons.topic: Talking about your daily routine as a teacher and finding time to study English.
lessons.lesson_task: The student will verbally describe their typical weekday to the tutor. The tutor will ask questions to help the student identify the best time to build a new study habit.

lessons.objective: The student can describe different places to study and explain what makes a good study environment.
lessons.topic: Describing the best places to study at home or in a cafe.
lessons.lesson_task: Role-play: The tutor acts as a friend asking for advice on where to study. The student verbally describes their favorite study space in their house and explains why it is better than other rooms.

lessons.objective: The student can name basic study tools and explain how they use them to learn English.
lessons.topic: Discussing the tools you use for your daily study habit.
lessons.lesson_task: The student will orally present three study tools they use to the tutor. The tutor will ask the student which tool is their favorite and how often they practice with it.

lessons.objective: The student can state simple learning goals and explain why they want to improve their English.
functional_language: I need to learn how to...
lessons.topic: Setting goals for your free time to become a better English speaker.
lessons.lesson_task: The student will speak about two short-term English goals. The tutor will play the role of an academic advisor and ask the student how these goals will help them in their daily life or travels.

lessons.objective: The student can talk about things that interrupt their studies and how to stay focused.
lessons.topic: Staying focused and avoiding your phone in a noisy place.
lessons.lesson_task: Role-play: The tutor will act as a student who is easily distracted. The student must verbally give the tutor advice on how to turn off distractions and take proper breaks.

lessons.objective: The student can ask for clarification and help when they do not understand a lesson.
lessons.topic: Asking questions during online classes when you need help.
lessons.lesson_task: Role-play: The tutor will read a short, slightly difficult sentence. The student must use functional phrases to interrupt politely, ask the tutor to repeat, and ask what specific words mean.

lessons.objective: The student can describe how they check their work and remember new English words.
lessons.topic: Reviewing your notes to improve your English memory.
lessons.lesson_task: The student will verbally explain their process for reviewing new vocabulary after a class. The tutor will ask the student how they fix a mistake when they find one.

lessons.objective: The student can discuss how they balance their job as a teacher with their English studies.
lessons.topic: Making a study plan for the weekend when you feel tired from work.
lessons.lesson_task: The student will verbally outline their weekend routine to the tutor, explaining how they balance family time, resting, and studying. The tutor will suggest adding one more hour of study, and the student must negotiate the plan.

lessons.objective: The student can give basic advice to others about building good learning habits.
functional_language: It is a good idea to...
I think it is useful to...
lessons.topic: Giving advice on how to review and learn new skills.
lessons.lesson_task: Role-play: The tutor plays a new English learner who is struggling to study. The student must verbally give the tutor three pieces of useful advice based on their own learning experience.

lessons.objective: The student can present a complete weekly study plan, detailing their habits, tools, and goals.
lessons.topic: Presenting your successful study schedule and goals to your tutor.
lessons.lesson_task: A guided discussion where the student verbally presents their ideal weekly study plan to the tutor, explaining their goals, preferred study spaces, and how they manage their time around teaching and family life. The tutor should prompt the student to use vocabulary and phrases from L1-L9, asking follow-up questions such as 'How do you avoid distractions?', 'When do you review your notes?', and 'What tools do you use to stay focused?'
